data.hypothesis: Adding only a compile-gated OpenMP SIMD directive to the existing indexed x loop tests whether an explicit vectorization hint helps without row-base hoisting. The prior valid row-base-plus-SIMD candidate measured 0.0813 seconds, while the no-directive pointer-induction candidate measured 0.4494 seconds; those differ in both access form and directive, so they do not isolate the cause. This candidate tests whether the directive alone helps, while retaining generic x bounds and making no alignment or ISA assumption.

memory_lessons.applicability: Stencil x-loop experiments in this campaign.
memory_lessons.claim: The valid row-base-plus-SIMD candidate measured 0.0813 seconds and the valid no-directive pointer-induction candidate measured 0.4494 seconds, but their access patterns also differ; these results do not establish the directive's independent effect.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this directive-only candidate against the indexed baseline and the prior row-base candidate, measuring both core budgets including setup.

data.notes: Only the x-loop directive is added. It is enabled when _OPENMP reports OpenMP 4.0 or newer; otherwise the original loop remains. No alignment, fixed vector width, compiler setting, initialization, recurrence, or boundary behavior is changed. Correctness and performance remain for the controller to validate and measure.
transformations: Added an OpenMP SIMD directive immediately before the existing contiguous-x loop, guarded by _OPENMP >= 201307.
Kept the original indexed accesses, recurrence expression, initialization, boundaries, and scalar fallback unchanged.
